name: One Recent Experience
summary: A research-conversation identity that favors a concrete recent event over general opinions or leading questions.

palette.name: Background
palette.evidence: Native Office page/sheet white ground; explicit design choice retaining the reading surface.

palette.name: Text
palette.evidence: used style Normal explicit text color

typography.usage: Titles and short section openings; source used style Subtitle.
Reading text, supporting labels and detailed explanations; source used style Subtitle.

recognitionRules: Use a plain Calibri document with a clear facilitator-copy label.
Put the time boundary and conversation scope near the title.
Separate primary questions from optional probes.
Leave note space between prompts and keep suggested interpretations out of participant-facing wording.

principles: Move from observation to interpretation to a bounded next question.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: Tell me about the last time you did that.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid “proves” when the material only supports a hypothesis.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: A record suggests a direction; it does not speak for every person.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use ONE RECENT EXPERIENCE as a small Calibri wordmark above a simple date line. No speech-bubble logo.
invariants: Use a plain Calibri document with a clear facilitator-copy label.
Put the time boundary and conversation scope near the title.
Separate primary questions from optional probes.
adaptations: A short interview may use fewer probes, keeping the same recent-event opening.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.
